why:
ours `(lifecycle_state_machine_t*, rclc_lifecycle_callback_t, void*)`, theirs `(lifecycle_node_t*, int (*)(void))`. Two differences, both accounted for. (1) The handle: theirs takes `rclc_lifecycle_node_t*`, ours `rcl_lifecycle_state_machine_t*` -- one handle instead of two, see `c:lifecycle_node_t`. (2) The callback SHAPE: rclc's is `int (*)(void)` with no context, ours is `uint8_t (*)(void *context)` -- `callback-bound-at-creation`. Constraint: no allocator, so a callback cannot capture; the context travels beside the pointer, exactly as it does for every other nros callback (`rcl_timer_callback_t`, `rclc_subscription_callback_t`).

HISTORY (issue 0792, FIXED): this row was a `gap` because the C DECLARATION was broken, not because of the shape. The Rust parameter was the cross-crate `Option<LifecycleCallbackFnCtx>`, and cbindgen -- which runs with `parse_deps = false` -- rendered it as an OPAQUE `typedef struct Option_LifecycleCallbackFnCtx Option_LifecycleCallbackFnCtx;` passed BY VALUE, so no C translation unit could form the argument to any of the twelve `*_register_on_*` entry points. A local `Option<fn>` alias, `rclc_lifecycle_callback_t`, now renders as a plain nullable function pointer -- the same shape `rclc_guard_condition_callback_t` already used and the same one the C++ shim's `nros_cpp_lifecycle_callback_t` always had. The ABI never changed; only the spelling did. The same cbindgen blind spot had also silently DROPPED all fifteen `NROS_LIFECYCLE_{STATE,TRANSITION,RET}_*` constants (each defined as a cast through an `nros_core` enum), so C had no name for a transition id or a callback return value either; they are now literals guarded by a `const _` assertion block against the Rust discriminants.
